The must-sees

10 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Church · 1900

    Alexander Nevsky Cathedral

    It was completed in 1900, when Estonia was part of the Russian Empire. In the 1920s there were plans to demolish it, but it was never torn down.

    Look for

    Turn round: the cathedral was placed squarely opposite the castle, then the seat of the Russian governor, as a sign of imperial power.

  2. 02
    Palace

    Kadriorg Palace

    Peter the Great started it in 1718 and named the park after his wife Catherine. It is now an art museum of foreign painting.

    Look for

    Behind the palace’s flower garden stands the office of the President of Estonia.

  3. 03
    Viewpoint

    Kohtuotsa Viewpoint

    From here the spires of St. Olaf’s and the Town Hall rise over red roofs, with the harbour beyond. The view is especially loved at sunset.

    Look for

    Look down on the steep red-tiled roofs of the lower town, packed inside the line of the old town wall.

  4. 04
    Museum

    Seaplane Harbour

    The hangars were built during the First World War for the Russian Empire’s navy. Inside, visitors can climb into the 1930s submarine Lembit.

    Look for

    On the quay outside lies Suur Tõll, a steam icebreaker built in 1914.

  5. 05
    Culture

    Song Festival Grounds

    The song festivals held here gather tens of thousands of singers. In 1988 crowds sang banned national songs here during the Singing Revolution.

    Look for

    Up the slope, a statue of the conductor Gustav Ernesaks sits looking down at the stage.

  6. 06
    Church

    St. Olaf’s Church

    In the 16th century its spire may have made it the tallest building in the world. Lightning struck it many times, and the spire burned more than once.

  7. 07
    Civic building · 1404

    Tallinn Town Hall

    Completed in 1404, it is often called the oldest surviving town hall in Northern Europe. The weathervane figure on the spire is known as Old Thomas, a guardian of the city.

    Look for

    Below the roof, find the dragon-headed waterspouts that carry rain off the walls.

  8. 08
    Civic building

    Toompea Castle

    The pink wing was added under Catherine the Great in the 18th century. Behind it, the medieval castle still has three towers standing.

    Look for

    At the corner of the castle rises Tall Hermann, the tallest tower. The Estonian flag on top is raised every morning at sunrise.

  9. 09
    Square

    Town Hall Square

    It has been the town’s marketplace since the Middle Ages. In December it fills with a Christmas market around a tall tree.

    Look for

    On the corner of the square, the Town Hall Pharmacy has been dispensing medicine since at least 1422, one of the oldest pharmacies in Europe.

  10. 10
    Museum

    Vabamu Museum of Occupations and Freedom

    It tells the story of Estonia under Soviet and Nazi German occupation, and of the return to independence. It was founded by Olga Kistler-Ritso, an Estonian who had fled to the United States.
